title: Repairing a Three-Way Light Switch: Wiring, Testing, and Troubleshooting
summary: An Ask This Old House segment demonstrates diagnosing and repairing a miswired three-way light switch that controls a chandelier from two switches. The hosts cover the anatomy of single-pole versus three-way switches, show how to identify traveler wires and the common wire using a continuity tester and a lamp accessory, and guide the viewer through safely turning off power, labeling conductors, wiring the three-way correctly (traveler wires to the traveler screws and the common wire to the common terminal), and testing the setup to ensure both switches control the fixture as intended. A wiring diagram is used to illustrate how a typical three-way circuit functions, helping homeowners understand why the miswiring prevented operation.
topics: two-switch control of a single fixture

sections.title: Problem setup and miswiring with a chandelier
concepts: three-way switch box with extra wires
sections.description: Pam asks about a problem where two switches control a single chandelier, and the box contains extra wires, indicating potential miswiring during three-way switch installation.

sections.title: Switch anatomy: single-pole vs. three-way
sections.description: The hosts introduce ground, contrast single-pole switches with three-way switches, and explain how the latter has three screws (two travelers and one common).

sections.title: Three-way circuit diagram and operation
sections.description: A diagram illustrates a typical three-way circuit: two traveler wires between switches and a common wire, showing how switch positions route current to light the fixture.

sections.title: Diagnosis plan: suspect miswired common/traveler
concepts: common vs traveler wires mixed up
sections.description: The host suspects the common and traveler wires are mixed and outlines a plan to correct the wiring.

sections.title: Safety and power-off verification
sections.description: Safety steps include shutting the circuit off at the panel and verifying absence of power with a voltmeter before touching wiring.

sections.title: Isolating and identifying conductors with a continuity tester
sections.description: Both switches are removed, and a continuity tester (with an internal power source) is used to identify traveler conductors by testing continuity between boxes.

sections.title: Confirming traveler wires and wiring plan
sections.description: The two traveler conductors are confirmed and prepared to be connected to the traveler terminals on the three-way switch.

sections.title: Final wiring test: correct three-way operation
sections.description: With power restored, the traveler and common conductors are wired to the correct terminals and the three-way switches are tested, demonstrating proper operation.
